name: rafeeq

scripts.ios:sync: npm run build:prod && npx cap sync ios
scripts.android:sync: npm run build:prod && npx cap sync android
scripts.android:build: npm run android:sync && cd android && set "JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr" && .\gradlew.bat assembleDebug bundleRelease
scripts.analyze: npm run build:prod -- --stats-json && npx webpack-bundle-analyzer build/stats.json

_browserslist_note: Floor is chrome 79, not a market-share query. `>0.2%` resolved `and_chr` to the single LATEST Android Chrome, giving zero coverage of stale WebViews on old devices — WebView updates via Play independently of the OS, so the OS version says nothing about the engine. 79 = the `max()` floor used by the --safe-inset-* tokens; below it safe-area layout breaks structurally. Capacitor 8 itself blocks below WebView 60 (android.minWebViewVersion), so 79 is the binding constraint. This governs JS SYNTAX transpilation only — newer CSS (color-mix, font-palette) is handled by per-declaration fallbacks and degrades gracefully, so do NOT raise this floor to match a CSS feature. See docs/webview-compat-audit.md.
